subject: URG: Production impact — cache eviction storm causing head-of-lane stalls
messages:
From: Sara Thompson <sara@acme-retail.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.ai>
Cc: ACME Oncall <ops@acme-retail.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production: sudden latency spikes and 5xxs on inference v2

Elliot —

We're seeing a major regression starting ~14:50 PST: latency for our image-captioning inference route jumped from ~120ms p95 to >2s and a 5xx tail (502 gateway errors) is spiking. This is affecting checkout recommendations and causing a 12% drop in throughput to our storefront.

Attached is a screenshot from our APM with a couple request IDs and a short heap of logs that show rapid cache eviction events: acme_latency-screenshot.png.

Can you confirm this is on Redwood's side? We need an ETA — this is driving revenue impact.

—Sara
Director of ML Engineering, Acme Retail

From: Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Thompson <sara@acme-retail.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 15:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden latency spikes and 5xxs on inference v2

Sara — thanks for the heads up and the logs/screens. I'm escalating immediately. Initial ack: we see elevated tail latency and gateway 502s correlated with heavy prefix churn in our KV cache for your tenant.

Action plan (short):
- I'm looping infra and SRE now (cc'd).
- Run targeted mitigations: reduce max_batch_size for Acme traffic, enable an emergency cache-pin mode to lower eviction pressure, and route overflow to a lower-memory model variant if needed.
- ETA for first mitigations: 30m. Will report back with metrics and request IDs.

We understand the impact — we'll treat this as P1 until resolved.

—Elliot
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.ai>, monica_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 15:35:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden latency spikes and 5xxs on inference v2

Quick triage notes — attaching traces and a short extract: kv-trace-20261119.txt, kv-stats-20261119.csv. Observations:

- We are seeing a ‘prefix eviction storm’: a small set of long-running prefixes with intermittent high diversity of request prefixes is causing the per-worker KV LRU to thrash.
- Thrash is provoking head-of-lane (HOL) blocking in batch lanes: large batches are waiting for KV lookups that are being evicted/repopulated by concurrent requests, causing stalls and cascading timeouts.
- Simultaneously, a hot partition on a subset of tenant routes is causing sustained async-io backpressure leading to gateway 502s when the request dispatcher exceeds the soft queueing window.

Immediate mitigations applied (in flight):
1) Reduce max_batch_size from 128 -> 32 for Acme route (low-risk, decreases HOL stalls).
2) Enable per-tenant cache pinning for most-frequent prefixes at worker-level (pinning threshold lowered).
3) Short-term routing: divert overflow to quantized model variant (smaller KV working set).

I opened JIRA PERF-4321 to track follow-ups: durable cache sharding and stronger tenant isolation on eviction.

I'll continue to monitor; sending metrics after the change.

—Markus
Director, Serving Runtime

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Thompson <sara@acme-retail.com>, Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.ai>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 16:00:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden latency spikes and 5xxs on inference v2

Sara —

We've pushed the first wave of mitigations (reduced batching + cache pin) at 15:50 PST. Early telemetry shows p95 on your route dropping from ~2s -> ~220ms and 5xxs decreasing to baseline. We'll keep the temporary config for 4 hours while we validate stability.

Can you confirm whether you see improvement on your end (even partial)? If you still observe 502s please share one or two failing request IDs and we'll pull server-side traces.

Also capturing this under the incident for post-mortem and credit evaluation.

—Monica
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.ai>
To: board@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Exec briefing: Acme incident (latency spike + cache churn)

Quick exec note for leadership:

What happened: a tenant-specific pattern of high prefix diversity caused aggressive per-worker KV eviction. That eviction churn produced head-of-lane stalls in batch processing lanes and overflowed our soft queueing window — visible to the customer as p95 jump and gateway 502s.

Impact: Acme storefront saw ~12% throughput loss for ~40 minutes before mitigations. Customer revenue impact estimated; Monica is capturing metrics and the credit ask.

Immediate response: reduced max_batch_size, enabled per-tenant pinning, routed overflow to quantized model variant. Incident resolved with temporary configs within ~30 minutes from detection.

Next steps (short):
- Permanent config: implement eviction-aware cache sharding and per-tenant soft quotas (owner: Markus, ETA: 2 weeks).
- Post-mortem and customer-facing RCA (owner: Monica, ETA: 48 hours).
- Comp plan: review credit/SL exception request and prepare a remediation timeline (owner: Elliot).

Please acknowledge. I'll circulate the draft RCA once Monica's doc is ready.

—Elliot
Head of Customer Reliability

From: Sara Thompson <sara@acme-retail.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: ACME Oncall <ops@acme-retail.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden latency spikes and 5xxs on inference v2

Elliot / Monica —

Thanks for the rapid response and clear mitigation steps. We saw performance recover to normal within ~20–30 minutes after your changes. Appreciate the pinning + reduced batching approach.

Please include the following in the RCA: exact post-change metrics, an explanation of why our request mix triggered the eviction storm, and your proposed timeline for a permanent fix. We'll likely request a one-time credit for the impacted window; Monica, please let us know the next steps and documentation required.

—Sara
